intro: FANN renovates villas in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, including kitchens, wardrobes, bathrooms, flooring and finishes. The proposal defines the areas being changed, joinery details, service interfaces, approval responsibilities and site access for the actual property.

sections.heading: Define the rooms and the existing condition
sections.text: Send the villa location, rooms or areas being changed, current photographs and any available drawings. Separate a kitchen or wardrobe upgrade from a wider renovation. Identify items to retain, remove or replace, and record anything that needs a site check before the scope is agreed.

sections.heading: Plan access around the household
sections.text: Say whether the property will be occupied during the work. Agree access, delivery routes, protection of retained finishes and how work areas will be separated. Review any phased handover or restricted working periods for this property rather than assuming the whole villa is available throughout.

sections.heading: Release kitchens and wardrobes against details
sections.text: Joinery needs agreed dimensions, materials, finishes and internal arrangements before production. Share appliance information and storage requirements, and identify items supplied by others. Record samples and drawing revisions so a later change can be reviewed for its effect on scope, cost and timing.

sections.heading: Assign services and approval responsibilities
sections.text: Bathroom, kitchen and lighting changes need clear interfaces with the relevant services. Identify who checks the existing condition, prepares drawings and handles any required community, developer or authority submissions. Record responsibilities and exclusions in the proposal rather than assuming a universal approval package.

sections.heading: Agree checks before handover
sections.text: Separate design decisions, production, site work and final checks in the programme. Set out the agreed finishes, responsibility for service testing, outstanding items and handover information. Review unresolved approvals, materials and supplier interfaces before treating a desired move-in or handover date as confirmed.

faqs.question: What should we send for a villa renovation quotation?
faqs.answer: Send the villa location, the rooms or approximate area being changed, current photographs and any available drawings. Identify items you want to keep, remove or replace, plus your preferred handover date. Separate confirmed choices from open decisions so the proposal can define the work and any checks still needed.

faqs.question: How should we plan work in an occupied villa?
faqs.answer: State whether the villa will remain occupied before the work programme is agreed. Discuss delivery access, protection of retained finishes, separation of work areas and any restricted working periods. If you need phased access to rooms, record that requirement in the brief rather than assuming every area can be worked on together.

faqs.question: What needs approval before kitchen or wardrobe production?
faqs.answer: Approve the joinery drawings, dimensions, materials and finishes before production is released. Share appliance details and the internal storage arrangement, and identify buyer-supplied items. FANN has a joinery workshop in Umm Al Quwain; project quantities, approved details and the programme determine the production plan, rather than a fixed universal lead time.

faqs.question: Who handles community, developer and service coordination?
faqs.answer: Agree coordination responsibilities for the actual villa and proposed changes in the project scope. Identify required drawings, who prepares and submits them, and who checks service interfaces such as plumbing, power and lighting. Existing conditions and review steps need confirmation before the site programme is treated as agreed.

faqs.question: How is a villa renovation handover planned?
faqs.answer: Plan handover around the agreed scope, approvals, materials, joinery and site access. Separate your desired completion date from confirmed production and installation milestones. Record outstanding items, responsibility for service checks and the information you need at handover, then review changes before relying on the programme for a move-in date.
